title: Man shot by police talked about 'suicide by cop': lawyer
article: A man who was fatally shot by police in Winnipeg last week talked about "suicide by cop" before he was killed, according to one of the officers' lawyers.
Howard Fleury, 34, was shot by police responding to a domestic complaint Friday night at a home on Alfred Avenue in Winnipeg's North End neighbourhood.
The police department won't officially discuss the details of the incident until their investigation is complete. At least two officers have been placed on leave while the case is investigated.

But Hymie Weinstein, who represents one of the officers on leave, has shared his client's version of events. Weinstein says his client told him Fleury's estranged wife met officers when they arrived and told them Fleury was out of control and carrying a knife.
Then, Weinstein says, his client says the officers were confronted by Fleury on the back steps of the North End home.

"The first thing basically out of his mouth [was], "Have you guys heard of suicide by cop?'" said Weinstein. The term "suicide by cop" refers to the actions of a person who would impel officers to use deadly force against him.
Weinstein says officers used pepper spray on Fleury once, then Fleury went inside and locked the door. Officers were about to force the door, he says, when a young girl opened it.
More pepper spray was used, the lawyer says, but Fleury kept advancing toward police until he was shot.

David Chartrand, president of the Manitoba Métis Federation, disputes Weinstein's characterization of events, saying he has spoken to Fleury's estranged wife, Kimberly Desjarlais, and heard a different story.

"Speaking with the wife this morning, following the comment by Mr. Weinstein, she's making it very clear: 'I was standing there. He never said anything of that nature. I don't know why this is coming out now.'" Chartrand said.
Chartrand says if Fleury wanted to die, officers should have called in a negotiating team, especially since children were in the house at the time of the incident.
